title: to ..., for ... and so that ...
subtitle: to do / for something / so that ...
summary: Use to + verb to say why somebody does something, for + noun for the thing you want, and so that (with can/could, will/would) to express purpose.

lesson.heading: to ... for purpose
lesson.text: **to + verb** (*to reserve ... / to make ...*) tells us the purpose of something: why somebody does something, has something or needs something, or why something exists.

examples.text: I called the restaurant **to reserve** a table.
What do you need **to make** bread?
We shouted **to warn** everybody of the danger.
This letter is **to confirm** the decisions we made at our meeting last week.
The president has a team of bodyguards **to protect** him.

lesson.heading: a place to park, something to eat, work to do
lesson.text: We use **noun + to ...** to say what something is for or what must be done with it. Sometimes there is a preposition (*on, with, to*) after the verb. We also say **money / time / chance / opportunity / energy / courage to do** something.

examples.text: It's hard to find **a place to park** in the city centre.
examples.note: = a place where you can park

examples.text: Do you have much **work to do**?
Is there **a chair to sit on**? I get lonely if there's **nobody to talk to**.
I need **something to open** this bottle **with**.
They gave us **money to buy** food. Do you have much **opportunity to practise** your English?

lesson.heading: for ... and to ...

left.label: for + noun
left.text: for tells us the thing we want.
examples: I had to run **for the bus**.

right.label: to + verb
right.text: to tells us the action we want to do.
examples: I had to run **to catch** the bus.

lesson.note: You can say for somebody to do something: There weren't any chairs for us to sit on, so we sat on the floor.

lesson.heading: for -ing and What ... for?
lesson.text: We use **for (do)ing** to say what something is *used for*. But we do not use *for -ing* to say why somebody does something - use **to ...**. You can use **What ... for?** to ask about purpose.

examples.text: This brush is **for washing** the dishes.
I went into the kitchen **to wash** the dishes.

lesson.heading: so that
lesson.text: We use **so that** (not *to ...*) especially with **can / could** and **will / would**. You can leave out *that*: *I hurried so I wouldn't be late.*

examples.text: She's learning English **so that she can** study in Canada.
We moved to London **so that we could** see our friends more often.
I hurried **so that I wouldn't** be late.
examples.note: = because I didn't want to be late

examples.text: I hurried **so** I wouldn't be late.

lesson.text: To explain why you do something, use *to + verb*: *I went out to buy milk* (not ~~for buying~~). Use *for + -ing* only to say what an object is used for.

exercises.prompt: I went into the kitchen ___ the dishes.
exercises.explanation: To say why somebody does something we use to + verb, not for -ing.

exercises.prompt: Match each action with its purpose.

pairs.right: to warn people of the danger.
to see what was in it.

pairs.left: I moved to a new apartment

pairs.right: to find out if they had any rooms free.
to help me with my work.

exercises.prompt: Would you like something ___? Coffee? Tea?
exercises.explanation: something to drink = something that you can drink.

exercises.prompt: I came home by taxi. I didn't have the energy ___.
exercises.explanation: energy to do something: I didn't have the energy to walk.

exercises.prompt: Does each sentence need to or for in the gap?

items.text: We'll need time ___ make a decision.
I went to the dentist ___ a check-up.
He's very old. He needs somebody ___ take care of him.
Can you lend me money ___ a taxi?
I put on my glasses ___ read the letter.
I had to run ___ catch the bus.

exercises.prompt: They've passed their exams. They're going to have a party ___.
exercises.explanation: to + verb gives the purpose of the party: a party to celebrate.

exercises.statement: I had to run for catch the bus.
exercises.explanation: I had to run to catch the bus (or: I had to run for the bus). Use to + verb for an action, for + noun for a thing.

exercises.prompt: I didn't want to get cold, so I wore warm clothes. I wore warm clothes so that I ___ cold.
exercises.explanation: so that + would/wouldn't: I wore warm clothes so that I wouldn't get cold.

exercises.prompt: I wanted Mark to be able to contact me, so I gave him my phone number. I gave Mark my phone number so that he ___ me.
exercises.explanation: so that + could: I gave Mark my phone number so that he could contact me.

exercises.prompt: I wanted the car behind me to be able to overtake, so I slowed down. Make one sentence with so that.
exercises.answer: I slowed down so that the car behind me could overtake.

exercises.prompt: I wish we had a garden ___ play in.
exercises.explanation: for somebody to do something: a garden for the children to play in.

exercises.prompt: Why are you so scared? There's nothing ___ afraid of.
exercises.explanation: nothing to be afraid of = nothing that you need to be afraid of.
